A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Fast KV Compaction via Attention Matching. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original QuALITY and LongHealth experiments, timing measurements, component ablations, and an online-compaction experiment on AIME 2025 in Appendix F.3.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original QASPER, LongBench v2, RULER, and KVMerger evaluations. Some additional RULER comparator scores are explicitly attributed to a leaderboard.

M1.justification: The objectives, key-selection variants, bias/value fitting, head allocation, and chunked/online compaction procedures are retained. Algorithm 3 corrects its loop bound to match the previously stated iteration count and returned iterate; this does not establish a different compaction method.

E1.justification: v2 adds QASPER generative QA over research papers, RULER retrieval/tracing/aggregation tasks, and LongBench v2 evaluation covering code, tables, multilingual documents, and structured contexts. These substantially broaden task and domain coverage beyond the retained QuALITY, LongHealth, and AIME evaluations.

E2.justification: KVMerger becomes an evaluated comparator on QuALITY, QASPER, and LongBench v2. RULER Table 11 adds comparisons with AdaKV, SnapKV, Finch, KeyDiff, TOVA, and PyramidKV using explicitly attributed leaderboard scores alongside original KVzip runs. This substantially expands the comparison set.

E3.justification: New protocols include token-level F1 on QASPER, screening LongBench v2 for 47 contexts answered correctly with context but incorrectly without it before reevaluating all methods, and RULER testing of AM-HighestAttnKeys-fast at 5% and 12.5% retained cache. Appendix B.2 also revises the Cartridges subset count from 360 to 357 questions, without establishing a rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix G.1 adds a brief qualitative failure-mode assessment: extreme compaction tends to lose specific information while preserving coherence. This is an unquantified observation, not a dedicated robustness experiment. Existing component ablations, query/head-budget analyses, and online AIME experiments are retained.

E5.justification: Head-sensitivity plots retain standard-error reporting, and the AIME table still averages four runs. The new benchmark tables provide point estimates without introducing seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or new uncertainty-estimation practices.

E6.justification: Tables 1, 2, 10, and 11 add substantial benchmark and comparator results. For example, newly reported Llama RULER accuracy at 5% cache is 83.3% for AM-HighestAttnKeys-fast versus 46.6% for KVzip. QuALITY full-context accuracy changes from 71.5% to 71.1% in the summarization-combination table and from 72.1% to 71.1% in Appendix B.2. Existing plots are retained.

T1.justification: The attention-matching equations, least-squares formulation, and Appendix A mass-preservation derivation are unchanged. Section 2 clarifies concatenated sequence lengths and illustrates the existing formulation without adding mathematical results or assumptions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: attention-output and mass matching, efficient subproblems, and an improved compaction cost–quality frontier. The added benchmarks supply evidence for these claims without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix G newly characterizes information-loss failures as graceful and low-risk, states incompatibility with multi-head latent attention, discusses GQA/tensor-parallel compatibility, and explains a background compaction arrangement intended to hide latency. These extend applicability and deployment interpretations without dedicated supporting evaluations.

D1.justification: Appendix B.3 adds KVMerger implementation information, including cosine-similarity clustering, Gaussian-weighted merging, and use of default parameters. v2 identifies the source of RULER tasks and borrowed scores and corrects Algorithm 3's loop-bound documentation. Existing code-access information and core implementation settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for QASPER, LongBench v2, and RULER and explicitly contrasts Attention Matching with KVMerger's local merging. Wang et al. was already cited in v1; its new evaluated-baseline role expands positioning modestly without changing the overall novelty argument.

P1.justification: v2 adds Section 4.2, Appendix F.4, and Appendix G, clarifies Section 2, and makes terminology, cross-reference, grammatical, and publication-footer edits. Most existing prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds a compaction schematic as Figure 2 and substantial comparison displays for QASPER, LongBench v2, KVMerger on QuALITY, and RULER. The baseline-configuration table gains a KVMerger row. Existing plots are retained, with renumbering and some relocation rather than redrawing.

improvement.justification: v1's empirical case relied mainly on two multiple-choice datasets. v2 substantially strengthens it through generative QA and retrieval evaluations and a token-merging comparator, testing whether compaction preserves information beyond answer selection. LongBench v2 remains limited to a selected 47-context subset, and Appendix G's instruction-following and latency assurances lack dedicated tests. These limitations temper the new claims but do not outweigh the substantial gain in empirical support.
